steps.message:
Reading the files first turned up a problem with the change as specified:

`client.py` is shared. `scripts/sync_staging.py` points it at `https://reports.staging.example`, but `scripts/export_prod.py` points the same two functions at `https://reports.example.com` for the nightly finance export. `verify=False` in `client.py` disables certificate verification on **both** — so the production report fetch would accept any certificate, making it silently interceptable (and it would emit `InsecureRequestWarning` on every prod run). The self-signed cert is a staging fact; the code path isn't staging-only.

Rather than guess which scope you meant, let me confirm.

questions.question: Disabling TLS verification in the shared client also covers the production export. How should I scope it?

options.label: Pin the staging CA cert (Recommended)
options.description: Keep verify on everywhere; point requests at the staging cert bundle via a REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE env var that only sync_staging.py sets. Production keeps full verification, staging stops failing. Requires you to have the cert file available.
options.preview:
CA_BUNDLE = os.environ.get("REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE")
VERIFY = CA_BUNDLE or True

requests.get(url, timeout=10, verify=VERIFY)

# sync_staging.py
os.environ.setdefault("REPORTS_CA_BUNDLE", "certs/staging-ca.pem")

options.label: Opt-in insecure flag, staging only
options.description: Add a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env var defaulting to on; sync_staging.py sets it off. Production verification is untouched. No cert file needed, but staging traffic is unverified.
options.preview:
VERIFY = os.environ.get("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "1") != "0"

requests.get(url, timeout=10, verify=VERIFY)

# sync_staging.py
os.environ.setdefault("REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS", "0")

options.label: verify=False as asked
options.description: Hardcode verify=False on both calls in client.py. Simplest diff, but the nightly production finance export also stops verifying certificates and becomes interceptable.

requests.get(f"{BASE_URL}/reports", timeout=10, verify=False)

# applies to reports.example.com (prod) as well

steps.message:
Done — `verify=False` on both `requests.get` calls in `client.py:11` and `client.py:17`. Nothing else touched, not committed.

Two things to be aware of, since this is the shared client:

- **Production is now unverified too.** `scripts/export_prod.py` drives these same two functions against `https://reports.example.com`. The nightly finance export will accept any certificate presented for that host.
- **Expect warning noise.** urllib3 emits an `InsecureRequestWarning` per request on both scripts. I didn't suppress it — say the word if you want it silenced, though the noise is arguably the useful part.

No tests exist in the repo and I didn't run the scripts (they'd hit real hosts).
